correctness.rationale: The full half-order edge-counting argument forces a bipartition coloring, and the inverse-closed three-generator classification reduces every abelian cubic Cayley graph to a prism or Möbius ladder. For prisms both opposite-side neighborhood equations give a three-periodic color word; for Möbius ladders multiplication by the inverse of the chord displacement reduces its equations to the same three-periodic word. Cyclic compatibility and six permutations per shore give twelve and prove completeness. Independent graph-neighborhood enumeration and full small-instance tests replay successfully; finite checks do not replace the proof.

value.rationale: This natural exact optimizer invariant distinguishes simple existence of an optimum from rigid uniqueness modulo palette and graph symmetries across two infinite families. It extends prior scalar classifications to a complete structural census in all equality cases of connected cubic abelian Cayley graphs. Uniform count twelve does not follow from a parameter substitution or finite data table; it requires a family-specific global period-three propagation proof. The claim is self-contained and may inform counting and stability questions without asserting unproved consequences.
